notes:
I couldn't write any of the notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

I tried to open eight pages at once: Enduring Word on Psalm 57, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, Precept Austin, Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org (Psalm 56 in his numbering), the NET Bible notes, and Spurgeon's Treasury of David on studylight.org. The research tool said I had no searches or page fetches left for this turn, so none of the pages loaded.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written notes from memory. They would have no real sources behind them and could misstate what these teachers actually wrote.

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll start by reading those pages verse by verse. Then I'll look up:
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** each tradition's own teachers on the allowed sites, such as Spurgeon, Wesley's notes and Ligonier.
- **Other views:** modern scholarship (Bible Odyssey and the NET Bible notes), Catholic and Orthodox readings, and any debated popular teaching the sites discuss.

The notes will go verse by verse ("v. 4: ..."), with a URL after each point, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
